title: Cinnamon pear porridge with fresh figs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, milk, pears, walnuts, figs, Greek yoghurt and honey are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every item is a Tesco staple, and a few fresh figs in season are an ordinary buy rather than a treat purchase.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan, a small frying pan and a grater, with simple stirring and toasting.

works.reason: 200g oats to 1 litre of liquid, simmered for 5 to 6 minutes, gives four generous bowls of creamy porridge, and the toppings are well judged.

honest_times.reason: Grating one pear, toasting walnuts and cutting fruit fits in 10 minutes, and 8 minutes covers bringing the pan to a simmer and cooking.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the cinnamon and salt, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Warm spiced porridge suits a cold end of October, and six quartered figs give each bowl a substantial fig topping rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling breakfast of oats, fruit, nuts and yoghurt with only a small drizzle of honey.
